extracted.intended_audience: college mathematics instructors (including graduate teaching assistants) who run in-class group activities and want students to read textbooks
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing, running, and assessing cooperative in-class group work and for encouraging students to read the mathematics textbook before class. Covers startup mechanics, time management, handling off-task behavior, facilitation practices, and reading-assessment techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give clear directions on what to do during group activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide very clear instructions on what activity you want the students to work on, and what you expect them to produce at the end of the activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write instructions on the board or put them on an overhead; give a brief account of the tasks students will undertake; communicate expectations about the product of the activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give clear instructions on how and where groups should form and what problem to work on
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell students exactly how and where groups should form and which problem they should work on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific grouping procedures (count off, alphabetical, birth date) and explicitly state the problem to be tackled so students don't default to off-task conversations or unrelated homework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set a definite pace and time frame for group work
rubrics_metrics.description: Set a definite pace for the group work, and give the groups a definite time frame in which to work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announce the allotted time before beginning; for long multi-part activities, break work into sections and stop to discuss completed parts; communicate schedule clearly to motivate timely engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visit groups while they work and give constructive suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: As the groups work on their problem, the instructor should visit each group and give suggestions on what approaches they may try.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a quick initial tour when activity starts to detect off-task groups and reiterate instructions; do not get too involved with any one group; acknowledge stuck groups and promise to return if you cannot assist immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrap up by having students explain answers
rubrics_metrics.description: When wrapping up the group exercise, have the students explain the answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call on groups to supply answers during wrap-up; have some groups read their answers or present at the blackboard to make work visible and hold groups accountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclude by listing the vital points addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: When concluding a group activity, briefly list the vital points that were touched on in that activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize key ideas to reinforce learning and connect the activity to course goals; use the conclusion to clarify misunderstandings and highlight important methods or results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanics for starting a group activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical startup steps to get groups focused and working on the assigned task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have one person in each group read the problem aloud; occasionally ask all groups to do the exercise at the blackboard; write instructions visibly; perform an initial classroom tour and immediately correct off-task behavior by reiterating exact expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deal proactively with off-task behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect and respond to groups that are not working on the assigned activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If groups persistently work on homework or are off-task, reassign groups; ask groups which parts they've completed and have them explain an answer; warn that groups will be called on during wrap-up; move underperforming groups to the blackboard to increase accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan additional activities for fast groups / early finishers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide follow-up activities for groups who finish the work very quickly so they remain productively engaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announce another problem and write a reference on the board; these need not always be explicitly introduced or wrapped up but should be available to engaged students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use time-splitting for long, multi-part activities
rubrics_metrics.description: For lengthy group tasks, break the work into sections and treat parts sequentially to keep pace and help slower groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stop class when most groups have finished designated parts (e.g., (a) and (b)), discuss those parts, then have students return to remaining sections; helps keep the desired pace and supports slower groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appoint a group facilitator to enforce schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a facilitator within each group who participates and ensures the group sticks to the schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The facilitator role helps maintain time management and encourages group responsibility without the instructor's constant intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and communicate ground rules for group conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Set explicit ground rules governing acceptable conduct during in-class group activities and communicate them often.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repeated communication to make clear that productive group functioning is important; address modes of operation, organizational issues, group dynamics, and individual responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange seating to promote interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure physical arrangement allows group interaction (e.g., four people facing each other) rather than seating that discourages discussion (e.g., four in a row).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If students move to different parts of the classroom, monitor seating so that structure supports dialogue and collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent monopolization of instructor time and irrelevant individual concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not allow individuals to monopolize instructor time with individual concerns or irrelevant issues during group activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defer grading/assessment questions to less public forums or require them in writing; keep in-class time focused on the group task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage participation and peer explanation rather than directive answers
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage dialogue among group members and elicit peer answers before giving direct solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one person is sitting out, ask them to explain the group's answers; determine if another student can answer before stepping in; avoid being overly directive in mathematical assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look for and intervene with non-working students
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify students who are not working on the assigned activity and encourage them to cooperate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt disengaged students to participate (e.g., ask them to explain their group's approach); use gentle, specific prompts to re-engage them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate the role of the textbook within course goals and assume pre-reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state how textbook reading fits course objectives and run class sessions assuming students have encountered basic vocabulary and techniques beforehand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate the textbook to lectures, activities, homework, and exams; tell students early what 'read the book' means; structure class to build on assigned readings rather than re-lecturing all material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define explicit expectations for what 'reading the book' entails
rubrics_metrics.description: Make clear to students what you expect when you say 'read this material before class' (examples include: memorize definitions/theorems; understand proofs; think about concepts; understand examples; have questions; be ready for discussion/quizzes/applications; relate material to prior reading; be able to explain/summarize/use new terms; do routine/complex problems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided checklist to communicate a mix of comprehension, application, and metacognitive goals; ask instructors to list what they want students to get from reading and share this with students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach students specific behaviors for reading mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Help students learn concrete strategies for reading math texts, such as making marginal notes, justifying steps, identifying assumptions, working out examples before looking at solutions, listing unanswered questions, re-reading, making summaries/outlines, relating sections to prior material, using Content-Form-Function outlines, asking the purpose of a discussion, and reading non-linearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate these behaviors in class; have students role-play instructor/student reading scenarios; remind instructors that students' reading skills differ from instructors' and that practice and modeling are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use role-play/modeling to teach reading techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Model and practice reading–teaching behaviors by having instructors role-play teaching students how to read a section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divide participants into pairs, have each take turns demonstrating reading strategies aloud and pausing to show when/how to use behaviors; if participants are reluctant, use observers or an experienced instructor demonstration but encourage practice whenever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess reading with techniques that are themselves learning experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Use assessment techniques that encourage regular reading and promote higher-level thinking rather than only factual retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize Bloom's taxonomy to design higher-order reading assessments; prefer assignments like submitted notes or summaries that double as learning activities rather than simple recall quizzes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading assessment techniques (specific methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete assessment methods to encourage and evaluate textbook reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods include: daily reading journals periodically read/commented by instructor; daily submitted questions on reading used to drive Q&A; section summaries (individual or pairs); e-mailing difficulties/questions prior to class to drive activities; pre-assigned reading questions with periodic quizzes; brief vocabulary quizzes asking students to explain new terms; collecting and assessing reading notes; assigning homework on material not covered in class; and testing reading by placing accessible new mathematics on a test that only readers could answer.
